- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 81.91) — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high and then correcting.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model fails to recognize when prices are drifting toward historical averages.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts are too optimistic when recent prices are rising sharply.
- When true price rises >10% from prior day, model often overcorrects by +5–10% beyond the true peak.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — tends to flatten prices too early.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 78.0 — model systematically adds +1.5–3.0 to mean.
